issues.description: Sample code claims 'Get the node' via `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` — relies on undocumented iteration order
issues.detail: The Basic Usage example writes `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` to retrieve the node just defined. This is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` but obscured behind a generator, and worse, it pretends a single-node pipeline is the general case. A reader copying this pattern into a multi-node pipeline will silently retrieve some other node. State the postcondition ("retrieve the node whose name is `train_model_node`") and write `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`. The current form is UNREASONED.

issues.description: Top-level `node(...)` calls appear outside any pipeline or function, presented as if executable
issues.detail: Several blocks (the Mermaid config example around the diagram, the Text preview code-highlight example, the closure example) end with a bare `node(func=..., preview_fn=..., name=...)` expression at module scope. As written this constructs a node and discards it; it neither attaches to a pipeline nor binds to a name. A reader following the documentation literally will produce code that has no effect. Either embed each call inside a `Pipeline([...])` literal as the first example does, or assign it to a variable that is then used. The precondition of the example ("this is a runnable snippet") is not met.

issues.description: `preview_from_dataframe` and `preview_from_polars` are presented as preview functions but take a DataFrame argument
issues.detail: Earlier the docs state plainly: "Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly. They're independent functions that you define." Yet the Table preview section shows `def preview_from_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> TablePreview` and `def preview_from_polars(df) -> TablePreview` as if these could be passed to `preview_fn=`. They cannot — `preview_fn` is invoked with no arguments by `node.preview()`. The example is internally inconsistent with the contract stated 100 lines later, and the closure section even exists precisely to solve this problem. The two helpers should either be rewritten as zero-arg closures (matching the closure pattern shown later) or explicitly labelled as "helpers you would wrap in a closure".

issues.description: ImagePreview example contains unreachable code after a `return`
issues.detail:
```python
return ImagePreview(content="https://example.com/correlation_matrix.png")

# Or a data URI for inline images
# return ImagePreview(
#     content="data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."
# )
```
The alternative is commented out, but it sits after an unconditional `return` inside the same function, which is misleading pedagogy: it suggests a function can do both. Split into two named functions, one per branch, so the reader sees two complete, reasoned alternatives instead of one function with dead code attached.

issues.description: Experimental warning links to a relative docs path that may not resolve from the rendered page
issues.detail: The warning admonition links to `../about/experimental.md`. Relative links inside MkDocs admonitions are fragile across navigation depths and section moves; if `docs/about/experimental.md` is later relocated or rendered under a different URL, the link breaks silently. Verify the link resolves in the rendered site and prefer the canonical docs URL or a MkDocs-resolved cross-reference.

issues.description: `polars` added to ignore.txt alongside existing `Polars` — unreasoned duplication
issues.detail: `Polars` is already on the ignore list; adding lowercase `polars` is fine, but the change is unexplained and suggests Vale is being silenced rather than the underlying style rule being understood. State the precondition ("the word appears lowercase in `df.head(5).to_dicts()` prose") in the commit, or fix Vale's case sensitivity once rather than per-word.

issues.description: PR checklist explicitly admits no tests were added and no RELEASE.md entry
issues.detail: Two checklist items are unchecked: RELEASE.md and tests. For a docs-only PR the test omission is defensible, but documenting a new public surface (`preview_fn`, `preview_contract` module, `node.preview()`) without a RELEASE.md note means downstream users will not be told the feature exists. Add the RELEASE.md entry under the appropriate experimental-features section.

issues.description: Documentation asserts behaviour of `preview_contract` types and `node.preview()` without a single executable verification
issues.detail: Every code snippet here is TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best — and in fact not even tested, merely written. The docs assert that `preview.to_dict()` exists on every preview type, that `CustomPreview` takes `renderer_key`, that `meta` accepts a `language` key for `TextPreview`, that `MermaidPreview` merges its config with Kedro-Viz defaults, and so on. None of these claims are anchored to a doctest or a linked test. Recommend at minimum a doctest harness over the basic-usage block and a citation to the source module where the contract is defined, so the documentation tracks the implementation rather than drifting from it.

issues.description: Best-practice item 5 — "Handle errors: Wrap preview logic in try-except if needed" — is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE advice
issues.detail: Recommending try/except as a general best practice without stating what the precondition is, what exceptions are anticipated, or what the caller should do on failure trains readers to swallow errors rather than reason about them. Either state the specific failure mode ("if your preview reads from a dataset that may be missing, catch `DatasetNotFoundError` and return a `TextPreview` describing the absence") or drop the bullet. A best-practice list should not contain advice whose meaning depends on "if needed".

review.summary: This is documentation for an experimental feature, and to its credit it is appropriately fenced behind an experimental warning. However the prose is REASONED only at the level of vibe — several code snippets fail their own stated contract. The Basic Usage example fishes a node out of a pipeline by undocumented iteration order; the Table preview shows preview functions that take DataFrame arguments, contradicting the explicit statement 100 lines later that preview functions receive no inputs; multiple `node(...)` snippets are bare expressions at module scope that construct and discard the node; the Image preview contains unreachable code after a `return`. None of the assertions about the `preview_contract` API are anchored to a doctest or source citation, so the documentation will drift the moment the implementation moves. The fixes are mechanical and the discipline required is precondition/postcondition thinking on every example block before it ships.
